newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt to put on trial owner of collapsed flats.
newsitem.headline: Egypt to put on trial owner of collapsed flats.

text.p: The owner of an apartment block that collapsed on top of its residents in Cairo last year, killing 64 and injuring 16, would be put on trial for manslaughter, sources at the prosecutor's office said on Wednesday.

They said Raouf Ibrahim, if convicted, faces up to life in prison with hard labour after he was charged with causing the death of building residents due to his negligence. The trial date has not been set.

The prosecutor charged Ibrahim with disregarding the original blue-print of the building and constructing pillars and infrastructure that were faulty. He was also charged with constructing five illegal floors on top of the block.
Three construction engineers who were remodelling a flat on the first floor of the building were also charged with removing vital supports and pillars which brought the building down.
The 11-storey building, located in the Cairo suburb of Heliopolis, collapsed into a mountain of rubble in late October, killing and trapping scores of residents.
The collapse, one of the worst to happen in Cairo, prompted the government to issue a decree which sends anyone to jail for illegally constructing floors or renovating a building.

High property prices in Cairo have encouraged landlords to add extra floors illegally. Several buildings have collapsed beneath the extra weight and recent earthquakes have also taken their toll on poorly constructed buildings in the crowded city.
